name: floating-action-menu
title: Floating Action Menu
description: A floating action button that springs open into a radial fan or vertical stack of quick actions, pinned to any corner of the viewport or a container. Implements the menu button pattern with arrow key navigation, Escape to close and focus return; items appear instantly when reduced motion is preferred.

whenToUse: Mobile screens with two to five primary actions
Editors and tools that need quick create actions
watchOut: Keep the button clear of bottom navigation and cookie bars
More than five actions belongs in a real menu

name: gradient-background
title: Gradient Background
description: An ambient backdrop of slowly drifting, blurred color fields with an optional grid or dot texture, wrapping any content as a children slot. Ideal for heroes, empty states and auth screens; decorative layers are aria-hidden and the drift stops when reduced motion is preferred or paused.

whenToUse: Hero sections and empty states that need atmosphere
Behind glass cards and pricing tables
watchOut: Keep text contrast high on top of moving color
Large blurred layers cost GPU on low end phones

name: logo-marquee
title: Logo Marquee
description: An infinite, seamless logo or text marquee with direction and speed props, edge fade masks, pause on hover or focus and an optional pause button. Duplicate copies are hidden from assistive tech; with reduced motion it renders a static wrapped list.

whenToUse: Customer and partner logo rows
Ticker style news or feature lists
watchOut: Duplicate content is hidden from screen readers, so keep one readable copy
Pause on hover so people can read it

name: magnetic-button
title: Magnetic Button
description: A call-to-action button that is pulled toward the pointer within a radius, with label parallax and a spring back on exit. The effect only runs for fine hover pointers and is disabled on touch devices and under reduced motion; the button stays a native, keyboard-accessible element.

whenToUse: One primary call to action on a hero
Playful portfolio or agency sites
watchOut: Use it once per page or it stops feeling special
Pointer only effect, touch users see a normal button

name: social-link-button
title: Social Link Button
description: A social profile link with built-in GitHub, X, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and email glyphs, where the brand color floods in on hover or focus. Comes as icon, pill or expanding variants with an accessible name and new-tab hint; the fill switches instantly under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Footers, profile cards and contact sections
Author bios on blogs
watchOut: Brand colors change, check each platform guide
Label icon only links with the platform name

name: spotlight-card
title: Spotlight Card
description: A card whose surface and border light up with a soft glow that follows the pointer, in solid, glass or outline variants with an optional subtle tilt. Keyboard focus inside the card centers the glow; tilt is disabled and fades are instant under reduced motion.

whenToUse: Feature grids and pricing tiers
Dark landing pages that need depth
watchOut: Glow is pointer driven, so keep the card useful without it
Too many glowing cards side by side compete for attention

name: tilt-card
title: Tilt Card
description: A 3D product card that tilts toward the pointer with a following glare and depth layers for image, title and price. Supports a link or action button; keyboard focus shows a ring and a subtle lift, and reduced motion keeps it flat.

whenToUse: Hero product shots and collectible style cards
Small grids of featured items
watchOut: Keep tilt subtle on cards with text
Disable on touch where it can feel jittery

name: animated-tabs
title: Animated Tabs
description: Tabs with a sliding indicator in underline, pill or browser-style folder variants, optional count badges for filter tabs, and panels that cross-fade on change. Follows the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern with automatic activation, arrow, Home and End keys; reduced motion swaps the indicator and panels instantly.

whenToUse: Splitting related content into peer sections on one page
Filter tabs that show result counts, like All, Open, Closed
watchOut: Only the active panel is mounted, so panel state resets when switching tabs
Automatic activation switches on focus; avoid it for panels that load slowly

name: border-beam
title: Border Beam
description: A wrapper that draws an animated border around any content in four styles: a travelling light beam, a rotating conic gradient, marching ants and a flickering neon glow, with configurable colors, duration, width and radius. The border is decorative and hidden from assistive tech; with reduced motion it renders as a static border.

whenToUse: Highlighting a featured pricing tier or call to action
Signalling that an AI input or job is actively working
watchOut: Beam and rotating rely on CSS @property, so very old browsers show a static gradient
Use on one element per view; several moving borders compete for attention

name: command-palette
title: Command Palette
description: A ⌘K / Ctrl+K command dialog with fuzzy search that highlights matched characters, grouped results, recent items, per-item shortcut hints, an empty state and a footer legend. Built as an ARIA combobox and listbox with arrow, Home/End, Enter and Escape keys, a focus trap, focus restore and body scroll lock; the opt-in global hotkey ignores typing in other fields, and reduced motion removes the scale and highlight animations.

whenToUse: Apps with many pages or actions that power users jump between
A single keyboard entry point for navigation, actions and settings
watchOut: The hotkey is global; disable it when another component already owns ⌘K
Fuzzy matching runs on the client, so very large lists should be pre-filtered or virtualised

name: loader-set
title: Loader Set
description: A family of seven loaders (orbit, bouncing dots, equalizer bars, ring spinner, pulse rings, infinity and a spinner that morphs into a drawn checkmark) sharing one size, speed and label API and inheriting color from currentColor. Each renders role="status" with sr-only text; with reduced motion they hold a static frame with a slow opacity pulse.

whenToUse: Indeterminate waits inside buttons, cards or full pages
Confirming a save with SpinnerToCheck once the request resolves
watchOut: Prefer a skeleton for waits longer than a couple of seconds
Set color with a text-* class on a parent since loaders use currentColor

name: notification-bell
title: Notification Bell
description: A bell button with a capped unread badge that pops on change and a shake when new items arrive, opening a popover with avatars, relative times, unread dots, mark all as read and an empty state. The panel is a labelled dialog with aria-expanded, Escape and outside click to close and focus return, and new arrivals are announced politely; reduced motion removes the shake and pop.

whenToUse: App headers that surface mentions, assignments and system alerts
Inbox style feeds where users clear unread items in bulk
watchOut: The component is controlled, so persist read state yourself in onItemClick and onMarkAllRead
Relative times use Intl.RelativeTimeFormat; pass locale to match your UI language

name: password-strength-input
title: Password Strength Input
description: A password field with a show and hide toggle, a four-segment strength meter whose fill and color track the level, and a live checklist of configurable rules that tick with a drawn check. Strength is announced through aria-live only when the level changes and the meter and rules are linked via aria-describedby; reduced motion fills and ticks instantly.

whenToUse: Sign-up and change password forms
Showing users exactly which password rules are still missing
watchOut: Rule-based strength is a hint, not real entropy; always validate on the server
Pass a stable rules array (module level or useMemo) to avoid needless recomputation

name: toggle-switch
title: Toggle Switch
description: An accessible role="switch" button with a spring knob that squashes and stretches while pressed, in default, day-night (sun to moon with sky gradient and stars) and icon (cross to check) variants, plus sizes, label, description and disabled state. Labels and descriptions are wired via aria-labelledby and aria-describedby; reduced motion removes the squash and springs.

whenToUse: Settings that take effect immediately, like Wi-Fi or notifications
A playful dark mode toggle with the day-night variant
watchOut: Use a checkbox instead when the change only applies after a form submit
Without a visible label, pass aria-label so the switch has a name
